title: Almond Field Protocol 2018 - FFAR/Bee Better Survey
author: Lauren Ponisio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rwwd7fe
materials: Each person should have the following field supplies prepared prior to starting a day in the field: 50 screw-top vials Spray bottle filled with ethanol Spray bottle filled with bleach + water (approx 10% bleach) Nitrile gloves (at least 5 pairs) Kestral with working batteries Stopwatch with working batteries Ziploc bags for specimen storage Sharpies Weather data sheets Net (wipe handle with ethanol before each round, or any time that you accidentally touch net with skin) Field lead should also have the following supplies: GPS with working batteries Falcon tubes Transect tape Flagging tape/pin flags Dry shipper/dry ice cooler

steps.title: Measure temperature and wind
steps.instruction: Turn the Kestral on by holding the centre button; shade the white temperature coil with your hand, use left/right buttons to reach the temperature screen, ensure units are °C (press centre+right to change), wait for stabilization and record the temperature (must be between 17 °C and 24 °C). Then face the wind, hold the Kestral perpendicular, go to the AVG windspeed screen, ensure units are m/s (press centre+right to change), wait for stabilization and record the average windspeed (must be ≤ 2.5 m/s) and the time of measurement.

steps.title: Set 30‑minute stopwatch
steps.instruction: Put the stopwatch in countdown mode (press centre mode button until countdown appears). Reset to 30'00'00 by pressing left split/reset; if reset does not show 30'00'00, press left and centre together until all zeros appear, then use left to toggle numbers and right start/stop to set minutes to 30, exit edit mode with centre. Start the countdown when sampling begins and stop it each time an insect is captured; keep it stopped while processing the insect, then restart for the next capture. Total active sampling per transect is 3 hours (9 hours per site) and can be split across days; alternate almond and hedgerow rounds at Bee Better sites.

steps.title: Put on and sterilise gloves
steps.instruction: At the start of each collection round, wear new nitrile gloves, wet them thoroughly with bleach, rub all surfaces, air‑dry, then wet with ethanol, rub, and air‑dry. Re‑sterilise gloves with bleach and ethanol whenever they become contaminated.

steps.title: Collect wild insects
steps.instruction: Search the transect for wild bees (excluding honey bees and Osmia), flies and wasps visiting flowers. When an insect is caught with the net, stop the stopwatch, place the insect in a labelled vial, sterilise gloves, then restart the stopwatch for the next capture. Do not talk while collecting and keep the vial away from your mouth.

steps.title: Record post‑sampling weather
steps.instruction: When the 30‑minute active period ends, use the Kestral to record temperature and windspeed again, following the same procedure as before.

steps.title: Label insect vials
steps.instruction: Write on each vial: Site code (or Site‑HR for hedgerow), transect number, bee type (if known), plant of capture (for hedgerow), date, and collector initials (e.g., WS2‑HR, Anthophora, Purple Sage, 2/12/18, KCT). Also label the cap with the site initials and HR if from hedgerow.

steps.title: Prepare Osmia emergence boxes
steps.instruction: Gather emergence boxes, punch one side hole (through both halves) and one top hole (if not already present), cover both holes with two layers of strong aluminium or steel‑reinforced tape. Store boxes with cocoons in a zip‑lock bag labeled “Osmia controls” and keep at –80 °C or in a dry shipper. For experimental cocoons, place 10 males and 10 females per vial, label with date and “Osmia control” and a “C” on the cap, then store similarly. Sort remaining cocoons into cardboard ‘jewellery boxes’ with 110 males and 110 females (or ratios specified by Jim Watts). Keep boxes refrigerated when not in use. Incubate all Osmia for exactly 5 days at 75 °F, starting 5 days before planned deployment.

steps.title: Sterilise net bags
steps.instruction: Soak net bags in a bleach‑water solution for 5 minutes on days off, rinse thoroughly, and allow to air‑dry overnight. Wipe net handles with the same bleach‑water solution on days off.

steps.title: Sterilise gloves (field routine)
steps.instruction: Wet gloves with bleach, rub all surfaces, air‑dry; then wet with ethanol, air‑dry. Re‑sterilise as needed and change gloves frequently. Avoid touching face, clothes or skin.

steps.title: Handle vials safely
steps.instruction: When opening any bag of vials, pour the vials onto a cleaned, sterilised surface (UV hood or sterilised tray) without reaching into the bag. Never touch the inside of a vial, do not breathe into it, and avoid speaking while handling.

steps.title: Gloves and forceps on arrival
steps.instruction: Upon arrival at a field site, put on nitrile gloves, sterilise the gloves and the forceps with bleach then ethanol as described above.

steps.title: UV‑sterilise nests
steps.instruction: Place each nest in a UV steriliser with holes facing up, run for 15 minutes, rotate the nest and run another 15 minutes. Perform UV sterilisation only a few days (or less) before field work and keep nests in their original boxes away from dead bee bodies.

steps.title: Prepare nesting holes
steps.instruction: Insert one liner into each nesting hole, label the nest side and roof with the site abbreviation using a Sharpie, write columns A‑G across the top row and rows 1‑14 (or 1‑13) down the side, creating a coordinate system for later vial labelling.

steps.title: Create no‑template control vial
steps.instruction: Take one vial, label with date, site abbreviation and the word “control”, write a “C” on the cap, hold the open vial to ambient air for 30 seconds, close it, and place it in a zip‑lock bag labelled “Controls”. Keep this bag available all day and store it in the dry shipper at day’s end.

steps.title: Collect Osmia from nest
steps.instruction: Wait at the nest until a female Osmia flies into a hole; place the rim of an empty vial against the hole so the bee backs into it and close the vial. If the bee does not enter, gently pull the liner and use sterilised forceps to capture the bee, then extract any pollen, larvae or mud from the tube on a clean work surface. Sterilise hands and forceps between each bee.

steps.title: Package collected Osmia vials
steps.instruction: After all bees from a nest are collected (≈1.5 hours), place the vials from that nest into a zip‑lock bag labelled with site, date, “Osmia”, and nest number. Use separate zip‑locks for each nest. When all nests are done, store the zip‑locks in a dry shipper; if vials must be kept longer before shipping, place them on dry ice to euthanise the bees humanely.

steps.title: Transport nests upright
steps.instruction: Carry each nest upright with the tubes facing upward; keep the front of the nest slightly tipped upward to protect larvae and pollen. Nests may be laid on their backs (tubes up) only for short periods during transport.

steps.title: Change gloves between sites
steps.instruction: Discard gloves after leaving a field site, put on a fresh pair, and re‑sterilise all gloves and equipment before starting at the next site.

steps.title: Label nest chambers
steps.instruction: From the back (oldest chamber) to the front, label chambers with lowercase letters a, b, c… and associate the mud wall at the back with the same letter.

steps.title: Establish transects and place nests
steps.instruction: Locate the three pre‑marked transects at each site (or establish them if absent). Space nests along the transects, away from each other and honey‑bee boxes. Label each nest with site initials on at least one side and a sequential number (e.g., WS Nest 1). Verify that the top of each nest shows columns A‑H and rows 1‑13/14.

steps.title: Select tree and affix nest
steps.instruction: Choose a tree with south‑ or east‑facing exposure and minimal dust, attach the nest using rope, wire or zip‑ties, and flag the tree with tape on the trunk and a branch.

steps.title: Install emergence box
steps.instruction: Place one emergence box on top of the binderboard (under the roof) or attach a tube to the nest with duct tape, then remove any tape covering the box holes.

steps.title: Apply pheromone spray
steps.instruction: Spray the nesting block with exactly 5 spritzes of pheromone spray to fully cover the nest, then record the GPS coordinates of the nest.

steps.title: Prepare mud if absent
steps.instruction: If no natural mud is present, mix site dirt with water in 2–3 plastic cups per nest, partially bury the cups in a dug hole, and keep the mud very wet (as some water will evaporate).

steps.title: Complete data sheet
steps.instruction: Fill out the site data‑collection sheet with all recorded information.

steps.title: Record Apis weather data
steps.instruction: Take weather data (temperature, wind, etc.) at the beginning and end of the Apis sampling period; only one person needs to record this for the whole period.

steps.title: Collect Apis bees
steps.instruction: Collect 10 Apis from each transect (30 per site). At Bee Better sites, collect 5 from almond rows and 5 from hedgerow; at control sites collect all 10 from almond rows. No timing required; simply capture the first 10 Apis encountered.

steps.title: Label Apis vials
steps.instruction: Label each Apis vial with: Site (or Site‑HR for hedgerow), transect, “Apis”, plant (for hedgerow), date, collector initials (e.g., WS1, Apis, 2/18/18, KCT). Label the cap with site initials and HR if from hedgerow.

steps.title: Store Apis samples
steps.instruction: Place all Apis vials from the three transects into a single zip‑lock bag labelled with site, date and “Apis”, then store the bag in the dry shipper.

steps.title: Collect flower samples
steps.instruction: Randomly select 5 trees per transect, collect 8 flowers from each tree (different parts of each flower, including petals, stamens, stigma), place all flowers from one tree into a single vial (resulting in five vials per transect). Avoid excessive petal loss; replace any flower that loses too many petals before entering the tube.

steps.title: Label flower vials
steps.instruction: Label each flower vial with: Site, transect, “Flowers Round #”, date, collector initials (e.g., HC3, Flowers Round 2, 3/1/18, KCT).

steps.title: Sterilise between flower trees
steps.instruction: Between trees, sterilise gloves and forceps with bleach, then ethanol, and flame‑sterilise the forceps once ethanol has dried.

steps.title: Store flower samples
steps.instruction: Place all flower vials from the three transects into a single zip‑lock bag labelled with site, date and “Flowers Round #”, then store the bag in the dry shipper.

steps.title: Prepare lab work surface
steps.instruction: Upon arrival at the lab, sterilise the work surface with bleach then ethanol, put on gloves, and sterilise gloves and forceps (bleach, ethanol, flame). Re‑sterilise gloves after each site and forceps after touching each nest component (pollen, larvae, mud).

steps.title: Open nest and loosen binding
steps.instruction: Select a nest, loosen the binding (remove roof with screwdriver if needed, cut zip‑ties), and open the nest.

steps.title: Consult Osmia datasheet
steps.instruction: Refer to the Osmia installation/removal datasheet under “bees collected” to identify which holes contain larvae or pollen.

steps.title: Assign cell letters
steps.instruction: Assign letters to cells from back (oldest) to front: a, b, c…; label mud wall at the back with the same letter. Do not reassign letters when a component is missing; skip missing components but keep the letter sequence.

steps.title: Separate nest components
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, pull each component (mud, pollen, larva) from a cell into separate labelled vials. Sterilise forceps between each component. Each vial contains only one component (e.g., mud a, pollen a, larva a, etc.).

steps.title: Label component vials
steps.instruction: Label each component vial with: Site, Nest Number, Tube Code, Cell Letter, Component (mud/pollen/larva), collector initials, and processing date (e.g., RB Nest 1, G7a pollen, KCT, 2/28/18). Use the processing date, not the collection date.

steps.title: Check remaining tubes
steps.instruction: After processing known cells, examine all remaining tubes starting from top‑left (A1), record any contents, and dispose of empty tubes. Keep careful track of tube positions.

steps.title: Clean tabletop between liners
steps.instruction: Between each liner, wipe the tabletop clean of debris, then sterilise the surface with bleach followed by ethanol.

steps.title: Store processed nest vials
steps.instruction: Place all vials from a fully processed nest into a zip‑lock bag labelled with site, nest number, date and “Nest Contents”, then store the bag in the dry shipper.

steps.title: Create molecular no‑template control
steps.instruction: Take one vial, label with date, site abbreviation and the word “control”, write a “C” on the cap, hold the open vial to air for 30 seconds, close it, place it in a zip‑lock bag, and also place a separate control vial into a Falcon tube; this must be done even if other controls are already collected.
